Expand public housing. Exempt it from GST. Mandate social housing in new developments. House essential workers near their jobs. And make rent-to-buy a reality so paying rent counts toward ownership.

See the plan: https://thehousingcharter.com.au

From stronger industrial rights to more apprentices on the job, last week the AMWU has secured important policy wins for workers - here are our top 5 picks, with more to come ✊
 
The next step is implementing these commitments into action.
Employers shouldn't be able to lock workers out indefinitely because they took collective action. We've secured the policy, now let's make it law.

Restrict the CGT discount and negative gearing on property. Taxvacant homes and short-stay rentals. Stop rewarding investors who stack up properties at the expense of workers who just want somewhere to live.

See the plan: https://thehousingcharter.com.au

The Housing Charter calls for a National Housing Commission. A permanent public authority to plan, coordinate, and deliver housing at scale. Because leaving it to the market gave us a crisis.

See the plan: https://thehousingcharter.com.au

That's a wrap up! 

Check out the AMWU delegation to the ALP National Conference ✊ Dozens of workplace leaders who were once on the shop floor across our manufacturing industries, raising the issues of our members. We're proud of our work in intervening in Labor to develop policies for workers.

There’s progress on a Fair Work Court, proportional lockouts, housing, apprentices, skills, jobs for workers in energy transition regions and more. We’ve made great progress, and now we start the work of making sure our elected leaders get on with their job and deliver change for our members and their communities. 

We will be building plans with delegates and allies to make sure this all happens ✊

Our AMWU delegation spoke across three days of the ALP National Conference, pushing for workers’ rights, secure manufacturing jobs and affordable housing ✊ As conference wraps up, we’re proud of the substantial changes we’ve achieved for our members.

AMWU delegates across our energy regions could not be clearer 👏 

Manufacturing is the essential pathway to a dignified, secure and net zero future for Australia. The immense skills and experience held by workers in energy, resources and heavy industry are a national asset. 

We must harness this existing capability to secure the new economy. This means actively facilitating the transfer of existing skills into new, high-quality, unionised manufacturing jobs. 

Read our Blueprint for Action: https://bit.ly/3RgfLqe

AMWU members achieve significant improvements in workplaces, day after day.

Every barrier that limits the entry, growth, retention of any worker – male or female, young or old – is a victory for the employer. 

Equity is not a burden; it is the foundation of our economic power. 

Read our Blueprint for Action: https://bit.ly/3RgfLqe

WIN FOR ALL WORKERS ✊

If your boss owes you money, you should not have to wait years to get it back. 

Employers have been deliberately using their deep pockets and high priced lawyers to stall, delay and drag out resolution to disputes to exhaust workers.

A Fair Work Court will provide simpler, fairer and faster justice for working Australians to resolve workplace disputes.

There's been misrepresentations of the AMWU in the media and what we stand for. 

The AMWU's key priorities are workers' rights, secure manufacturing jobs and affordable housing.
